newsitem.title: GERMANY: GOLF-WOOSNAM BIDS TO EDGE FURTHER AHEAD OF MONTGOMERIE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOOSNAM BIDS TO EDGE FURTHER AHEAD OF MONTGOMERIE.

text.p: Defending champion Ian Woosnam regards the German Open starting on Thursday as a perfect opportunity to edge further ahead of arch-rival Colin Montgomerie and move closer to a third European rankings title.

In the absence of fellow Briton Montgomerie, who came second in the U.S.Open on Sunday, Welshman Woosnam, currently leading the rankings, will try to distance himself from the reigning European number one.

"I was a bit inconsistent a the end of last year," said Woosnam, who finished second behind Montgomerie on the order of merit as the Scot won his fourth successive title. "And I really had a bad back at the end of the season so I had no real chance to put pressure on him," he added.
Woosnam still suffers from his back but he hopes that a curious health-cure recommended by Spain's Severiano Ballesteros will help him on his way.
The 1991 U.S. Masters champion started wearing a copper bracelet to ward off back pain six weeks ago, and found it helped.

"The bad back never goes away but -- touch-wood -- I'm clear of problems this week," he said. "I felt a twinge just picking up my bags coming here but the copper ring which Seve advised me to use did the business."

Woosnam said he still expected a tough challenge from fifth-placed Montgomerie until the end of the season but he sounded confident about his chances of finishing the year in the European number one spot.

"This year, I'm a lot more consistent and I've got well in front of him but he's always the man to beat," Woosnam said. "He's come into form recently, so no doubt he'll be up there again this year. If I can win this week, that will put a lot of distance between him and me at least, even if there are a lot of other good players who are just behind me."
As well as the metal bracelet, Woosnam perseveres with a similar metal driver to the one which got him into trouble on his way to missing the cut in the U.S. Open.

"They've toughened up this course with much heavier rough but it's not a patch on last week," added Woosnam, one of the critics of the controversial Stuttgart course, which was made more severe since several competitors said it was too easy last year.
Woosnam's main rival in Stuttgart could be Germany's Bernhard Langer, seeking a sixth win in this event. But Langer also missed the cut in the U.S. Open and is not completely clear of back problems.
Langer refused to blame his bad back for his poor play in Maryland, admitting his swing was more responsible than his unsatisfactory preparation.

Another one to watch will be Italy's Costantino Rocca, returning after injury forced his withdrawal from the U.S. Open. He will be attempting to halt his slide down the European Ryder Cup points table.
Zimbabwe's Mark McNulty, who finished tied 28th in the U.S. Open, will not be in Stuttgart because of a neck injury.
